svg.title: The Cajal-Meets-Transformer Synaptic Plate
svg.desc: Three-column Dawn State anatomical plate comparing recurrent transformer circuits across Inkling-2-Mini (K=3), Varloop (K=1..7), and Huginn-0125 (3.5B, K=1..8): Column I shows the Stem soma, hard somatic reset relay, and Huginn linear recall tether; Column II shows the braided QxK coincidence-detector synapse, Sage Green V and MLP twin backup cables, balanced non-normal shear loop ring, neuromodulatory gamma inverted-U curve, and orthogonal safety spectral separation; Column III shows private rotated loop waves refracting through the 6-layer Coda optical prism across the Fisher cliff versus Huginn's thin 2-layer Coda.

g.text: ARCHITECTURAL OVERVIEW | BIOPHYSICAL CIRCUIT ANATOMY OF RECURRENT TRANSFORMERS
How recurrent layers combine hard somatic resets, braided QxK synapses, non-normal shear, and a Coda prism.
Stem L0..L5 holding clean prompt memory
Hard somatic reset reloads Stem memory every pass
Reloads clean Stem activations on every pass
Continuous recurrent axon + linear recall tether
Recovery integral at K=8: −0.0491; tangent damp 0.142x
Synergy (state x recall): +4.453 nats at K = 8
II. THE 4 SYNAPTIC DENDRITES & BALANCED RECURRENT LOOP
Shared Recurrent Block (L6..L17) | Exact 16-Mask WHT Epistasis & Non-Normal Shear Law
Neither Q nor K alone suffices for multi-hop
Payload outweighs routing on both models
Isotropic noise contracts while one orthogonal mode amplifies
Top-8 Pass-2 modes vs safety basis:
Rotates private loop waves into vocabulary logits
Computation stays hidden until the 6-layer Coda
Thin readout lens; decoding occurs inside the loop
Non-normal shear still universal: Step 1 sigma_max = 7.63
Figure Notes: Comparative biophysical anatomy across Inkling-2-Mini (K = 3, 6-layer Coda), Varloop (K = 1..7, 6-layer Coda), and Huginn-0125 (3.5B, K = 1..8, 2-layer Coda).
Empirical scope: n = 120 multi-hop reasoning (WHT Parseval error <= 7.11e−15) and n = 64..128 safety & spectral suites (0.00e+00 unrolled logit diff).
